body: Copper Property CTL Pass Through Trust, the special-purpose entity formed in JCPenney's 2020 bankruptcy to hold the retailer's real estate, sued Onyx Partners, a Boston-based private equity firm, and its founder, Anton Melchionda, on Aug. 25, 2026 in Massachusetts Superior Court, The Real Deal reported, citing Bisnow. Copper seeks at least $150 million in damages.

Onyx agreed a little over a year earlier to buy the 119-store JCPenney portfolio, which covers more than 15 million square feet in 35 states, for $947 million. The deal was expected to close in early September 2025 but did not. By the end of the year, after a deadline was allegedly missed, Copper backed away, and Onyx sued Copper seeking to recover part of the $5 million deposit, arguing it was ready to close once issues on the seller's side were resolved.

Copper's complaint alleges Onyx lied about its cash on hand and "repeatedly misrepresented the status of funding discussions with major financial institutions to make their financing prospects appear more certain than they were." It says Onyx's failure to close cost the properties value and kept Copper from selling them to someone else. Copper also accuses Melchionda personally of deceiving it about the firm's ability to close and of using media leaks to Onyx's advantage.

Onyx has not given up on the deal. Last month it submitted a new $934 million bid for the 117 stores that remain in the portfolio, and it said it "looks forward to putting the litigation behind it, resolving the outstanding matters and moving swiftly toward closing the transaction." The stores operate under long-term leases, and a sale of the real estate is not expected to affect them.
